structured.approach: I read feat.tasks to find the Data Engineering tasks: TSK-01 and TSK-02, both in ap_pipeline. For each one I checked whether it needs any external access. Then I looked at the ap_pipeline code: I read ingest.py and pipeline.py to see how data comes in, read schedule.json, and searched the whole checkout for credential patterns (os.environ, getenv, secret, token, password, api_key, credential). I compared what the tasks need with the permission-table tool view, which says nothing is required or granted. Since nothing is needed, there is no gap and no access request. I used no connector, because the inputs and the code answered the question. The scheduling runtime is not covered by the inputs, so I raised it as a non-blocking open question.

claims.text: The Data Engineering tasks for FEAT-ZD-48600 are TSK-01 (STORY-01) and TSK-02 (STORY-02), both in the ap_pipeline repository.
TSK-02 is a pure function with no I/O, and TSK-01 builds on synthetic feed v3 rows. Feed v3 in production (PQ-6) gates release, not coding.
The pipeline entry point run(csv_text) takes the feed as text and opens no connection.
Ingestion parses CSV text from memory with the standard library csv module.
ap_pipeline uses the Python 3.9 standard library, and CI is the local command /usr/bin/python3 ci.py.
No secrets are required or granted for ap_pipeline. Required and granted match (both none), so no access request is needed and there is no excess access.
schedule.json defines a daily run at 02:00 Asia/Kolkata and references no credential.
ingest.py, pipeline.py and schedule.json are on TSK-01's must-not-change list, and a transport layer would re-trigger DES-01.

open_questions: SSQ-1 (non-blocking): schedule.json defines a daily run, but the inputs do not say which runtime executes the schedule or whether that runtime needs its own credential for the production feed. This should be re-checked at DE-13; it does not affect TSK-01 or TSK-02.
structured.summary: I wrote task.secrets_scope.md for FEAT-ZD-48600. The two Data Engineering tasks, TSK-01 (paid_date in the transform) and TSK-02 (the delays_by_vendor function), are pure-Python changes to ap_pipeline tested on synthetic data. They need no secrets in any environment. The permission-table tool view grants none, so required and granted match, there is no gap, and no access request was raised. The file also says when this check must be re-run and records one non-blocking question about credentials for the schedule runtime at DE-13. There are no blocking questions.
